To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of schools that are in possession of a computer has increased substantially in the past 4 yr, that the use of a computer in the classroom has also increased in this period, but that this increase is not due to an increase of computer use in the curriculum.

(1) computer use is very much dependent upon the teacher; (2) the use of computers is not embedded in existing curricula of the school; (3) teachers are not very enthusiastic about the use of computers in education; (4) teachers do not have a clear picture of the possibilities that the computer offers in the classroom; and (5) teachers have no clear idea about the goals that can be reached with the use of computers.
the use of the computer in primary as well a secondary education is still very limited.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to stimulate the use of computers in primary and secondary schools in such a way that it will be embedded in the curriculum and not just a personal interest of a few teachers.
the question whether computers in primary and secondary schools are a matter of individual interest of teachers or a matter of policy.
the question: How can we stimulate the use of computers in education?.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
computer usage in Dutch primary and secondary education is not yet a policy issue.
the computer is not yet fully integrated in Dutch education.
computer usage is still a matter of the individual teacher and is not yet part of a school policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computer is not yet a part of the educational system, but is a tool that is being added to the existing system.
the use of computers in education is still in an explorative and developmental stage.
computer use in primary and secondary schools is still in a very early phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of computers in the classroom is a process that needs time.
there are no clear indications that schools have developed a policy for the use of computers in education.
there is still a lot to be done in order to get computers in primary and secondary schools to be used in a meaningful way.
